contrary_evidence: Çatalhöyük 2024 20-building sample finds no enduring institutionalized wealth hierarchy but does identify temporary inequality and differentiated access to non-staple goods.

131 sampled ancient genomes in the 2025 Science study demonstrate maternal-line connections and changing burial-house kinship; they do not directly prove a female government, legal inheritance rules or universally sex-biased community migration.
2019 PNAS cranial injury observations (25 of 93, 12 with repeat injuries) identify interpersonal harm but do not identify state police, a professional army or the motives for each injury.
Subperiosteal skeletal reactions decrease 33%, 26%, 19% across Early/Middle/Late samples despite maximal crowding in Middle phase; density cannot be the sole infection mechanism.
Eastern Anatolian obsidian came from sources over 600 km away; geology does not reveal whether exchange used marriage, gifts, merchant intermediaries or direct travel.
UNESCO heritage East Mound occupation 7400–6200 BCE differs from detailed analytical period convention 7100–5950 cal BCE; different models and strata should remain explicit.
limitations: The UNESCO 37-hectare property includes both mounds and cannot be interpreted as the simultaneously occupied settlement area or a population census.
The plotted 400, 200 and 550 year phase lengths derive from coarse published analytical boundaries, not independently determined occupation lengths of every building.
Two health charts show different osteological indicators and denominators; values must not be pooled into a sitewide disease incidence rate.
Cranial injuries with recurrent trauma are a subset of the 25 injured individuals among 93 analyzed; the chart bars cannot be added.
Gini-style archaeological household proxies from 20 comparatively excavated buildings are not observed currency income distributions.
Ancient genetic kinship captures biological relations among sampled buried people, not adoption legal status, religious offices or political leadership.
Obsidian-source provenance is not direct evidence of a trade contract, merchant expedition or market price.
Source verification is based on directly accessible academic sources and cited summaries, not external scholarly peer review.

producer_checks.information_cutoff: 3 November 2026, America/Sao_Paulo. Includes academic research published in 2019, 2024, 2025 and a 2026 synthesis on matrilocality; literature sources all visible and individually identified in bilingual bibliography.
producer_checks.editorial_novelty: Fourth scheduled study (Block A item 4), a geographically focused Çatalhöyük monograph distinct from prior worldwide forager mobility and Neolithic origins comparative dossiers.
producer_checks.visual_signature: Four matching charts per language: Early/Middle/Late phases [400,200,550] years, skeletal lesion prevalence [33,26,19] %, dental caries by period and sex [10.5,9.7,12.9,10.0,10.4,11.0] %, cranial trauma sample non-additive [25,12] of 93; one evidence-limit matrix, four-chain causal diagram, seven-region evidence map.
producer_checks.source_check: 17 equivalent bibliography URLs in both versions across 10 independent hosts. Core numbers cross-checked in Larsen et al. PNAS 2019, Twiss et al. PLOS ONE 2024, Yüncü et al. Science 2025 and UNESCO heritage; obsidian provenance checked against archaeological journal abstracts.
producer_checks.bilingual_parity: 22 substantive sections and 1 bibliography each; matching 17 URLs and citation numbering, 4 identical numeric chart series, same major factual and methodological qualifications, equivalent table, map and flow.
producer_checks.research_depth: Each locale has over 5,400 substantive words and 42,000 characters, 22 chapters, critical comparison of contrary archaeological interpretations and auditable numeric charts.
producer_checks.methodology: Stratigraphic, bioarchaeological, paleogenomic, archaeological-architecture, dietary and geoarchaeological analysis. Separate observable quantities from hypotheses of property, authority, migration, inequality, political coercion and ritual meaning.

en.title: Çatalhöyük: houses, kinship, ritual and power in a Neolithic society without a documented state
en.deck: A detailed social, economic and political reconstruction of Çatalhöyük: food and household production, rooftop architecture, kinship DNA, burial and ritual, interpersonal violence, health costs, obsidian exchange and the evidence for episodic rather than institutionalized inequality.
keywords: Çatalhöyük houses roof access and burial
en.regime: Neolithic Çatalhöyük combined agricultural production, enduring house histories, maternal-line social relationships, selective access to prestige goods and recurring ritual, but the excavated evidence does not establish a permanent state-level hierarchy or universal economic equality.
en.key_risk: Conflating female-line genetic relationships with legal matriarchy, cranial trauma with organized armies, household food stores with state taxation, and Gini-like archaeological proxies with measured incomes or enduring class structure.

pt-BR.title: Çatalhöyük: casas, parentesco, rituais e poder numa sociedade neolítica sem Estado documentado
pt-BR.deck: Reconstrução econômica, social e política de Çatalhöyük: produção e alimentação domésticas, arquitetura sobre telhados, DNA e parentesco, sepultamentos e rituais, violência, saúde, trocas de obsidiana e desigualdade episódica em vez de hierarquia institucionalizada.
pt-BR.regime: Çatalhöyük combinava agricultura, memórias duradouras das casas, relações sociais por linhagens maternas, acesso diferenciado a bens de prestígio e rituais recorrentes, sem que a evidência comprovasse hierarquia estatal permanente nem igualdade econômica universal.
pt-BR.key_risk: Confundir vínculos genéticos maternos com matriarcado jurídico, traumatismos com exércitos organizados, estoques domésticos com tributação e indicadores arqueológicos semelhantes ao Gini com renda medida ou estrutura de classes permanente.
